scope: Bounded SQLite revision-publication spike; not a production schema

observations.name: WAL pinned snapshot survives whole-revision replacement
exception rolls back deleted and partially inserted rows
injected-cancellation rolls back deleted and partially inserted rows
deleted cache rebuilds identical canonical rows from the same graph
workspace annotation survives cache rebuild and becomes explicit orphan after target rename

limitations: Synchronous single-process experiment with separate SQLite connections; no worker or process crash was tested.
Cancellation is an injected AbortError at a transaction checkpoint, not actual worker cancellation.
cache.db and workspace.db have independent transactions; cross-database reads/writes are not atomic.
Annotation resolution uses exact extracted node IDs only; renamed/removed targets become orphans, with no automatic identity migration.
Canonical row equality is tested, not SQLite file-byte equality, scale, throughput, fsync durability under power loss, or production migrations.
